attentionItems.title: Rest Interval Violations Across Fashion Consultant Shifts
attentionItems.description: 8 Fashion Consultants (Emp02, Emp135, Emp158, Emp178, Emp188, Emp245, Emp257, Emp267) recorded rest intervals of 9 hours on 2026-10-02 through 2026-10-15, violating labor compliance thresholds (<11 hours minimum). Affects shift continuity and employee fatigue risk.
attentionItems.whatsHappening: Attendance roster shows systematic 9-hour rest intervals for evening-to-morning shift transitions, indicating either scheduling compression or clock-out/clock-in timing misalignment. This violates standard 11-hour rest requirements and creates fatigue liability.

evidence.title: Emp02 (HR DEPARTMENT) - 2026-10-06
evidence.desc: Morning shift 09:09–16:34 (6.8 hrs productive) with 9.0 hr rest interval following evening shift

evidence.title: Emp135, Emp158, Emp178 - 2026-10-15
evidence.desc: Evening shifts with consecutive 9-hour rest intervals, indicating back-to-back scheduling without compliance buffer

possibleCauses.title: Shift Scheduling Compression
possibleCauses.description: Roster planning algorithm may be prioritizing coverage over rest compliance, particularly for evening-to-morning transitions. Fashion Consultant demand spikes may force back-to-back scheduling.
possibleCauses.evidence: Evening shift clock-outs (20:37–21:05) followed by morning clock-ins (08:55–09:12) create 9-11 hour gaps; systematic pattern across 8 employees suggests policy-level issue, not individual variance.

decisionOptions.title: Implement 11-Hour Rest Buffer Enforcement
decisionOptions.description: Modify roster scheduling system to enforce minimum 11-hour rest intervals between shifts; block evening-to-morning transitions for same employee within 24-hour window. Redistribute load across part-time/contract staff (Emp84, Emp225, Emp393).
decisionOptions.impact: Eliminate compliance violations; reduce fatigue-related productivity loss (~4–6% recovery); mitigate labor law exposure.

decisionOptions.title: Audit & Correct Clock Records
decisionOptions.description: Investigate whether 9-hour intervals reflect actual scheduling or data entry/clock system errors. If legitimate, escalate to legal/compliance for remediation plan and back-pay assessment.
decisionOptions.impact: Clarify compliance posture; identify system gaps; protect against regulatory penalties.

attentionSummary: Fashion Consultant cohort (28 active employees, 2 resigned, 1 on notice) shows critical rest-interval violations affecting 8+ staff and productivity gaps of 24% below scheduled hours. Compensation equity variance of 205% ($18K–$55K) combined with attrition rate of 10.7% (3 exits vs 5% target) signals retention and fatigue risk across sales operations.
